Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 472 is a genuine bargain for a flexible friends' escape, and it fits my 547 budget. I am keen for an optional break after six months without leisure travel, and the group can use this departure. The destination has little pull, but at this price the trip itself is worthwhile, so I would book rather than save.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 4 bought at the 472 fare and 12 declined. Eight declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections. Four declines cited low trip interest or a strong outside option, and two of those explicitly called 472 affordable. The four buyers called 472 a bargain or meaningful saving. No customer objected to the fare itself, and the current price already equals the permitted cap, so there is no room to test higher.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 472 fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly one-quarter member conversion, with declines driven mainly by low trip interest and budget/inventory constraints rather than fare objections; conversion materially above or below this band would contradict it.

analysis.summary: Sixteen members responded at a 449 HKD fare. Six bought the member fare, all citing strong value and destination appeal; most said they would decline the 590 HKD regular fare. Seven declines were inventory/budget forced, and three were low interest or low destination appeal despite the fare being affordable. No customer objected primarily to the 449 price itself. The fare sits below the 472 cap, and capacity is not binding. Evidence points to testing a higher fare on fresh customers rather than lowering it.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus 449 HKD, since current buyers cite value and several decline the 590 regular fare.

analysis.summary: At the 282 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections; three were optional-trip disinterest with the fare described as affordable. All buyers cited the low fare as decisive, and two would even pay the 590 regular fare. No customer objected to the fare itself. Evidence points to the current fare being attractive, but buying at 282 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because buyers cite the fare as a strong bargain well below their stated ceilings.

analysis.summary: At the current 289 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought, all citing the low fare as decisive; most said they would decline the 590 regular fare. Declines were driven by low trip interest, recent travel, optional-trip appeal, or unavailable inventory, not by the fare being too high. No customer objected to price. This supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers to see whether receipts rise without losing too many buyers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will increase basic ticket receipts relative to 289 HKD, because current buyers cite the fare as a bargain well below their stated budgets and no decline was price-driven.

analysis.summary: At the 333 HKD member fare, 5 of 16 customers bought and 11 declined. Most declines cite low trip interest, recent travel, or keeping time and money for other optional trips, not the fare itself; several call 333 HKD affordable or a bargain. Five declines are environment-forced (no available ticket within budget). Price is rarely the binding objection, so evidence does not clearly support lowering the fare further.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because most declines cite low trip interest rather than price.

analysis.summary: At the current 298 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought the member ticket, citing the fare as a compelling bargain well below the 590 HKD regular fare and within budget. Three declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were voluntary-trip objections with low interest or recent travel, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. The fare sits well below the 472 HKD cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
